sections.20.4.52: BLOCK HEADER has a layout handle only in R2000 and later.
sections.20.4.84: LAYOUT has an associated block-record soft pointer in the common handle tail.

producer.lineage: DWG codec descends from ACadSharp; this is not an independent ACadSharp or native AutoCAD witness.
producer.generation: Create R13/R14 null and bound SHAPE with following 3D LINE, then reopen each with the producer and save in its original version; no binary patch or fixture committed. The producer reader reconstructs its missing layout registration before resaving.

scratchReceipt.scope: generated producer controls, no native semantic claim

validation.repeatability: Two fresh generator runs produced identical hashes for all eight DWGs.
validation.independentReader: GNU LibreDWG 0.14 JSON reads each resaved input. Each has one NOD ACAD_LAYOUT entry, a dictionary owned by the NOD, two uniquely named and owned LAYOUT entries and two distinct associated BLOCK_HEADER records. R13/R14 BLOCK_HEADER JSON has no layout member.
validation.cli: For all four resaved files, strict and explicit-partial, ASCII and binary output attempts failed without changing a pre-existing sentinel (16 attempts). Bound files have no entity or object failures but reach LAYOUT/BLOCK_RECORD backlink rejection; null files have a SHAPE parse failure and strict refusal, and explicit-partial reaches the same backlink rejection.
validation.earlierReaderObservation: Producer reopen sees one SHAPE and one LINE in each source; candidate parser publishes the later LINE on the null controls.

limits: ACadRust reconstructs the root in memory; the initial authored drawings did not contain that registration. This cannot establish native producer behavior.
The spec defines a forward reference but does not by itself prove every target DXF mapping or consumer interpretation; do not simply bypass reciprocal output validation.
Null SHAPEFILE validity, complete source and output graph closure, successful partial output, independent readback, and same-adapter corrected retry remain unproved.
